items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: [(note)] Ken was interviewed at the Jerome Jazz Party in Aspen, Colorado on October 10, 1997, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

ctx.x: Tenor saxophonist/clarinetist Ken Peplowski is one of the younger generation of jazz musicians who excels in the small group swing genre. He was born in Cleveland on May 23, 1959, and began playing professionally while still in his teens. Ken played with the Tommy Dorsey Orchestra, led by Buddy Morrow, and soon after with Benny Goodman’s last big band. He has recorded frequently on the Concord label, often with vocalists Rosemary Clooney and Mel Torme. Howard Alden is a favorite bandmate and the two appear in…
Ken was interviewed at the Jerome Jazz Party in Aspen, Colorado on October 10, 1997, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
We are filming today in Aspen, Colorado, and it’s a great pleasure for me to welcome Ken Peplowski, clarinetist and tenor saxophonist.
